laneWideFindings: SONG-CONTAMINATION RULE, CORRECTED 2026-09-28 (third data point, es-MX). My rule was 'add a word naming the intent, not the particle'. WRONG — that was never the variable. The unifying mechanism across all three languages is: THE DISAMBIGUATING TOKEN MUST NOT ALREADY APPEAR IN THE INCUMBENT VERTICAL'S OWN TITLE PATTERN. Portuguese worked because the additive particle is absent from lyric-page titles. German failed because the particle is inside the song title ('Und ich vermiss dich auch'). Spanish fails because 'significado' is inside the lyric sites' own URL/title template — letras.com/<artista>/<id>/significado.html, and 'letra y significado' is a standard page title, so adding it moved the SERP from streaming results to lyric-MEANING results and on Google made it worse. PRACTICAL TEST before choosing any disambiguator on a contaminated SERP: search "letra y <token>" (or the local equivalent) and see whether the incumbents already own that string.

MY CLAIM OVERTURNED: I told the head-explainer row that the emotional sense of "miss" is the youngest. FALSE. Etymonline dates "perceive with regret the absence of" to c.1300 and "fail to be in time for" (miss the train) to 1823 — three senses are YOUNGER than the emotional one. The Spanish intensifier row authenticated the Leipzig endpoint by reproducing de = 4,228,124 rank 1 in spa_news_2011_3M and labelled it Spanish correctly. FRAMING OVERTURNED on i-miss-you-too-in-spanish: I claimed Spanish cannot postpose the additive particle the way English postposes "too". FALSE — a 120-sentence Tatoeba census of attested también found 36.7% initial, 33.3% medial, 30.0% clause-final, and both ¡Te extraño también! and ¡Te echo de menos también! are attested. The CONCLUSION survives on a different mechanism: the asymmetry is pronoun OPTIONALITY, not particle placement. Spanish may omit the subject, so writing yo is elective and therefore contrastive, while English must write I every time and is left with the ambiguous clause-final too. Leipzig supports it — yo falls from rank 229 (news) to 1,761 (Wikipedia) while también barely moves.
